clusters.name: Walter's move to Sorrel Valley, 1952–1953
clusters.reason: Around Walter's move across the country to buy an apple orchard in March 1952, within the year: June's anxiety rose as she wrote to her sister Edna every day, homesick; Walter distanced from June, spending long hours in the trees; Glen fought at his new school and was sent home twice; Walter cut off from his brother Harlan over their father's land money; June's functioning fell and she kept to her bed for weeks that first winter; Walter and June fought over money for new trees; and by September 1953, when June joined the church choir and her letters to Edna thinned out, her anxiety dropped and her functioning rose, marking where the period settled.

clusters.name: Walter's orchard failing, 1968–1969
clusters.reason: Around the orchard's failure in May 1968, when a late frost took the whole crop and the bank called in the loan, within the following year: Walter drank heavily most nights; he and Glen blamed each other for the loan and were in conflict; Glen and Marian overfunctioned, taking over the family's money and the talks with the bank; Glen's son Carl's asthma attacks worsened that winter; Nora began wetting the bed in April 1969; Ida's heart trouble was found and she was told to stop working; and by October 1969, when Walter stopped drinking and took work pruning other men's trees, his functioning rose and the period settled.

clusters.name: Glen's job lost at the cannery, 1975–1976
clusters.reason: Around Glen's job lost when the Ridgeport cannery closed in February 1975, within the following year: Glen's functioning fell as he sat out of work most of that year in the truck in the yard for hours; Glen and Marian fought loud fights at night over money; Marian overfunctioned, taking a second job cleaning offices at night; Nora stopped eating properly and lost weight that summer; Nora distanced from Marian, keeping to her room and saying little; Walter began drinking again after six years off it in December 1975; and by June 1976, when Nora ate again and made the track team, her functioning rose and the period settled.

clusters.name: Wilma moving into Nora and Hollis's house, 1990–1991
clusters.reason: Around Wilma selling her farm and moving into Nora and Hollis's house in January 1990, within the following year: Nora and Wilma clashed over the children's bedtimes and meals; Hollis worked late and kept out of the kitchen rows, distancing from Nora; Hollis took his mother's side; Owen had tantrums at preschool and was sent home twice; Wilma overfunctioned, taking over Lily's care; Nora's eczema flared on both hands; Nora and Hollis fought most nights; and by June 1991, when Wilma took a flat in town, and August 1991, when Nora's eczema cleared, the period settled.

declined.reason: An acute episode: a few days from the wildfire's arrival on 12 August 1994 to the family's return home by 15 August, with the family calm again once home and the children back at school that week; the real threat passed and everyone settled within days.
